newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Halla Group in Australian steel venture.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Halla Group in Australian steel venture.

text.p: South Korea's Halla Group said on Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Resource Equities Ltd of Australia to form a joint venture to produce hot briquetted iron and steel pellets.
Under the memorandum, Halla also agreed in principle to a $430 million contract to build the venture's plant on a turn-key basis, a Halla executive said.
Lee Tae-keun, a director of Halla Group, said a final contract was expected to be signed late next year.
The joint venture will be capitalised at about $200 million and Halla will hold a 40 percent stake, Lee said.

The venture's plant, to be constructed in Australia's Mount Gibson area between January 1998 and the early next century, will have an annual production capacity for two million tonnes of hot briquetted iron and five million tonnes of pellets, Lee said.
Hot briquetted iron is a low-cost substitute for scrap iron and is widely used in manufacturing steel plates, a Halla statement said.
Halla plans to import part of the plant's products and supply them to a steel plate plant which Halla plans to build in South Korea, Lee said.
Halla Group has 17 member firms, including Halla Cement Manufacturing Corp and shipbuilding firm Halla Heavy Industries Co.
